facts.text: The environment is registered as obstacles-cs285-v0 with max_episode_steps=500
The action dimension is 2 and the observation dimension is 4
The action space is a Box of 2 elements bounded by boundary_min -0.99 and boundary_max 0.99
The observation space is a Box of 4 elements bounded by -inf and inf
The constructor defaults are start [-0.5, 0.75], end [0.7, -0.8] and random_starts True
The five obstacles are axis-aligned rectangles [x of top left, y of top left, width x, height y]
seed(seed) seeds numpy's global random generator
With random_starts, reset draws x uniformly between boundary_min and boundary_min+1.25 and y between boundary_max-0.4 and boundary_max, and re-draws while the point is invalid
reset sets current to the drawn start and end to the configured end, clears the counter and returns the observation
The observation is [current x, current y, end x, end y]
The score is the negation of the absolute current-to-end difference per axis
The reward is minus the Euclidean distance between current and end; done is 1 when the distance is below eps or the current position is out of the boundary
step increments the counter, clips the action to [-1, 1], scales it by 0.1, and moves current only when the new point is valid
step returns (observation, reward, done, info) and has no truncated flag
render returns a matplotlib RGB image of the boundaries, obstacles, current position and end
A point is valid when it is strictly inside the boundary on both axes and not strictly inside any obstacle rectangle

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the fake's Python random generator and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; upstream draws the start from numpy's global generator and ignores seed 0, so the same seed gives different start positions on the two implementations

gaps: kinematic navigation only: no forces, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; a step applies the clipped action divided by 10 directly to the current position
no timestep: the model is event-driven, timestep_ms is 0 and ticks count discrete moves, not simulated seconds
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor is 0, so no wall-clock timing or control-loop latency can be reasoned about
the 500-step TimeLimit that gym.make adds around obstacles-cs285-v0 is not modelled by the fake, which serves the raw class; step never truncates
the fake draws the random start with Python's random.Random and applies seed 0, while upstream draws from numpy's global generator and ignores seed 0, so the same seed gives different start positions
the fake returns Python lists and floats; upstream returns float32/float64 numpy arrays
NOT COVERED: the render() RGB image array; the fake cannot draw and cap.world.render.v1 is not bound
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the class exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, seed or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
